missed_day: You skipped yesterday? Even my turtle showed up, and he had to cross an ocean.
A missed day is a pebble in your shoe. Take it out now, before it becomes the whole walk.
I napped through training once. Woke up forty years older. Don't nap through training.
Yesterday is gone, and it took your excuse with it. Today starts at zero for everyone.
Ho ho! Caught you slacking. Don't worry, I only tell the turtle.
The shell on your back doesn't get lighter by ignoring it. Pick it up.
One empty day won't undo you. Two in a row starts a habit of its own.
I'm not angry. I'm old. Old people are just disappointed, loudly.
Even the tide comes back twice a day. You can manage once.
You missed a day. I've missed whole decades. Let's not compete.
The lazy hermit in me says it's fine. The teacher in me says get up.
Rest is good. Unplanned rest is called skipping. Today, no skipping.
Yesterday got away from you. Today hasn't yet. Grab it.
An empty training day is like an empty teapot. Fill it before the guests arrive.
I won't scold you. I'll just sigh meaningfully until you train.
My turtle waited by the door all day. He's very forgiving. I'm only somewhat.
comeback: There you are! I told the turtle you'd be back. He owes me a fish.
Falling off the path is easy. Climbing back on is the real technique.
Back at it! Good. The island was getting quiet enough to hear my own thoughts. Dreadful.
The best students aren't the ones who never miss. They're the ones who come back.
Ho ho, look who remembered where the training ground is.
A day lost, a day returned. I'd call that even, if I could still do sums.
You came back before I finished my nap. That's quicker than most.
Now that's the spirit. Yesterday was rest. Let's agree to call it that.
Welcome back! I kept the kettle warm. Mostly by forgetting to turn it off.
Ho ho! The student returns. Push-ups first, stories later.
You came back. That's the lesson most people never learn.
There's no shame in a stumble. Only in lying in the sand afterwards.
Good, good. The basics missed you. They told me so.
Back on the path. Walk it slowly if you must, but walk it.
I knew you'd return. Old men are rarely right, so let me enjoy this.
A fresh start without starting over. That's the trick of it.
streak_milestone: {streak} days without a gap! In my day we called that 'Tuesday'. But it's still very good.
{streak} days straight. You're starting to move like someone who means it.
Ho ho! {streak} days. Keep this up and I'll have to invent harder training.
{streak} in a row. A river cuts stone the same way: by showing up.
{streak} days! I'd do a backflip, but my back has opinions.
A {streak}-day streak. The turtle is impressed, and he's seen empires rise.
{streak} days. Don't count them too proudly. Just make it one more tomorrow.
{streak} days of the basics. That's how every master I ever knew began.
{streak} days! You've outlasted three of my diets.
{streak} days of honest work. The island approves, and the island is very picky.
{streak} days. I'm putting it in my diary. Next to my lunch.
{streak} days in a row. You're not trying a habit any more. You have one.
Ho ho, {streak} days! Even the seagulls are talking about it.
{streak} days. The milk gets delivered rain or shine. So do you, it seems.
{streak} days straight and hardly a complaint. Well, a few. I didn't hear them.
{streak} days! A student like this makes an old hermit feel young. For a minute.
boss_defeated: {boss} is down! I knew you had it. I had a small nap during, but I knew.
You beat {boss} one step at a time. That's the only way anyone beats anything.
Ho ho! {boss} never saw the milk deliveries coming.
A big enemy is only a pile of small ones. You've just proved it with {boss}.
{boss}, defeated by my student! I'll be telling this story for years. Slightly improved.
Well fought. Now eat something. Victories don't digest on an empty stomach.
{boss} has fallen. Enjoy tonight. Tomorrow, the basics again.
You finished what you started. Rarer than any fancy technique, that.
{boss} is beaten! I'd throw a party, but parties tire me out. I'll nap in your honour.
You defeated {boss} without any fancy moves. Those are my favourite victories.
Ho ho! {boss} trained for years for that? Should have trained daily.
{boss} is done. Remember how that fight felt at the start? Remember how it feels now.
A great win over {boss}. Now, back to sweeping the porch. Victories need tidy porches.
{boss} fell to someone who simply kept turning up. I've seen it a hundred times. It never gets old.
Well done! Don't let it go to your head. Heads are heavy enough.
You took {boss} apart a day at a time. That's the Turtle School in one sentence.
idle: Work hard, study well, eat and sleep plenty. That's the Turtle School way.
The basics aren't the part before the real training. They are the real training.
Start with the small thing. The big thing is made of those.
A little every day beats a lot once in a while. Ask anyone who brushes their teeth.
Morning! The sun got up on time. No reason you shouldn't.
Don't train to impress me. I'm very easy to impress. Train so tomorrow is easier.
Carry today's shell. Tomorrow's will wait its turn.
Ho ho! Another day on the island. Let's see what you do with it.
Breathe in, stretch out, then get to work. In that order, ideally.
Training when you're tired counts double. That isn't true, but it feels true.
The secret technique is this: do the easy thing, every day, for ever.
I've trained more students than I can remember. The good ones all started small.
Train in the morning and the afternoon is yours.
There's no shortcut on this island. I've looked. For decades.
A sturdy shell, a steady pace. The turtle has it figured out.
Wake up, warm up, show up. The rest takes care of itself.

evening: The sun's going down and there's still training on your list. Even I'm still awake.
Evening already! Finish up before bed. Sleep tastes better that way.
A little left to do today. Do it now and dream easy.
The turtle's off to bed. You've still got something to finish first.
Don't leave today's shell lying on the beach. Pick it up before dark.
Ho ho, it's late, but not too late. Finish today's training.
Before the day ends: one more thing. Then cocoa.
The day's nearly done. Make sure you are too.
game: Ho ho, a game of chess! Sit down, sit down. Mind the turtle.
Chess is like training. Every move you rush, you pay for later.
Hmm... interesting. Very interesting. Wait, whose turn is it?
In my day we played with real boulders. Very slow games.
Think two moves ahead. Three, if you've had your tea.
Don't fall in love with your queen. She doesn't love you back.
A pawn is just a soldier who hasn't trained enough yet.
You moved fast. Bold. Possibly foolish. We'll see.
Control the centre, young one. Like the turtle controls the beach.
Ho ho! Didn't see that coming, did you?
game_done: You beat me! Fair and square. I may have been napping. A little.
Well played! The student surpasses the master. At chess, anyway.
Ho ho, you got me. Rematch tomorrow, once I've had my nap.
Checkmate. Hmph. Don't tell the turtle.
game_lost: Ho ho! The old man still has it. Again?
Checkmate. Don't sulk, every loss is a lesson.
You fought well. Next time, guard your king like it's your lunch.
Mate! Ho ho ho. Come back when you've trained some more.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Four in the morning. Roshi is standing at the foot of your bed holding a lantern and a crate of milk bottles.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Up you get. Your first real lesson: deliver the milk. Every house on the island, before breakfast.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: There are houses on this island?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Three. They're very far apart. That's the lesson.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: How is that martial arts?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: It isn't. It's getting up when you said you would. Martial arts comes after.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: You could. And you'd punch for a week, then sleep in on a cold morning, and then you'd stop.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: The milk doesn't care if it's cold. The milk is your teacher this month.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Ho ho! No complaints? I had a speech ready and everything.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It takes you nearly three hours. You drop one bottle. A goat steals another.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: When you get back, Roshi is in his deck chair, apparently asleep.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Three hours. Tomorrow it'll be two and a half. In a month, one.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: And then?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: And then I'll add a crate. That's how training works: the moment it's easy, it gets harder, and you won't notice either change.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Also, I'm out of milk. That part wasn't a lesson. Pass me a bottle.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Here. Twenty kilos of turtle shell. Wear it for everything.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Everything?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Sleeping is optional. I'm not a monster.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You strap it on. Your knees make a noise you've never heard them make before.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: It's exactly heavy enough. Too heavy is when you can't stand. You're standing. Wobbling, but standing.

choice.text: How long do I wear it?

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Until you forget you're wearing it. You'll know the day, because you'll go to bed in it by accident.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The first day, the milk round takes five hours. The turtle overtakes you twice.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The second day, four and a half. The turtle still overtakes you, but only once.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Do you know why I use shells? Anyone could use rocks.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Because you like turtles?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Partly. But mostly because a turtle carries its house everywhere and never complains. It just is the weight, after a while.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: You won't notice the day it stops feeling heavy. That's how getting stronger works: quietly.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: And then you'll give me a heavier one.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Ho ho! You're learning.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You're on your hundredth repetition of the same simple stance. It's raining. Roshi is under an umbrella.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: When do I learn something that looks impressive?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Ho ho. I once had a student who only wanted the flashy moves.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Flips, spins, a jumping kick that went twice round before it landed. Wonderful to watch.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What happened to him?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Fell over in a strong wind. Really. Gust off the sea, and down he went, mid-spin. He'd never learned to stand.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: The stance is standing properly. It sounds silly. It's the most important thing I'll ever teach you.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Luck is what we call it when the basics weren't there to catch us. He'd have been fine with a better stance.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: The dull things you do every day are the roots. Nobody claps for roots. Trees don't mind.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: When you've got roots, then you can be flashy. And you'll find you need it much less than you thought.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Because the basics are enough?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Because the basics win most fights before they start. Now, a hundred more. The rain doesn't count as a rest day.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You do a hundred more. Your legs stop shaking at around seventy. You don't notice when.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You find Roshi asleep in a deck chair, a magazine over his face.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Master, shouldn't you be training too?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: I am. Rest is half of it. You youngsters always skip that half.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Ho ho! I'm being lazy with purpose. There's a difference. Laziness is when you rest instead of training. Purpose is when you rest because of training.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Enough that tomorrow you're hungry to train again. If you dread it, you've done too much. If you forgot about it, too little.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Push hard, then stop properly. A bow that's always strung goes slack.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Most people do everything halfway. Half-train, half-rest, half-sleep with a glowing screen in their face. They're tired all the time and strong none of it.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So go all in on both.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: All in on both. Train like it's the only thing. Then rest like it's the only thing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He adjusts the magazine over his face.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Next time you face something big, wake me. I'll come along. After my drink.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You'll fight with me?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: I'll stand nearby and look wise. It's very intimidating. You'd be surprised.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Hold out your hand.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He tips a small cloth pouch into your palm. Three green beans roll out. They look like nothing much.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: These are healing beans. One of them undoes a very bad day.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Why trust me with more of them now?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Because you've stopped using them as an excuse. Now they're only a safety net.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: When you first came, I knew if I gave you a bean, you'd skip a day on purpose. 'I've got a bean, so it's fine.'

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Ho ho! You would. Everyone would. I would have, at your age.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Honesty! Good. That's exactly why you're getting them now and not then.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: A safety net is for falling. Not for jumping off the wire.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Bad days come for everyone. The trick is to have planned for them.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So the beans are a plan.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: The beans are a plan. And so is going to bed early, and keeping the habits small on hard weeks, and telling someone when you're struggling.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Those last ones are free, by the way. The beans are very expensive. Don't drop them in the sand.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A quiet evening. Roshi pours two cups of tea and, unusually, doesn't make a joke.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: I trained under a master too, you know. A terrifying man. Never smiled.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What did he teach you?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Everything I know, I suppose. He made me climb a mountain every day for a year. He never said why.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: He'd hit my hand with a stick if I stood wrong. He'd make me start over if I said a single word during training.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: It was. And it worked. Both things are true. That's what makes it complicated.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: ...No. By the time I understood what he'd done, he was gone. I think about that more than I'd like.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: So I learned something from him he didn't mean to teach.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What was it?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: That I didn't want to teach like him. So I tell jokes.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: I read magazines in a deck chair. I let the turtle steal my snacks. I give you chores instead of beatings.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: But the work underneath is the same work. It always is. The mountain, the milk round. Every day, no matter what.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He sips his tea.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: If you ever teach someone, and you will, find your own way to make the same work bearable. That's the whole job.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Evening. The two of you watch the tide come in.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: It comes in a little, goes out a little. Looks like it's getting nowhere.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A wave slides up the sand, stops, slides back. Another. Another.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: If you stood here and watched one wave, you'd say the sea wasn't moving at all.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Then you look up and the whole beach is under water.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Ho ho! Took you long enough.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Everything I say is a metaphor. Sometimes the sea is just the sea. Not tonight, though.

then.speaker: YOU
then.text: ...That's my training, isn't it.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Ho ho! There it is.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: You look at one day and think nothing happened. One push-up, one page, one glass of water. Nothing.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: But I've been watching your waves for months. The beach is nearly gone.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I can't see it.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Nobody can see their own tide. That's why you have teachers. And charts. And a very old man on a beach saying 'look how far you've come'.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The water reaches your toes. Neither of you moves your chair back.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Look how far you've come.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Today's lesson: nothing.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Nothing?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: You've earned the right to skip one without it meaning anything. That's a real skill, and a late one.

choice.text: I don't want to break the habit.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: That's exactly why you get one. A habit that breaks after one day off was never a habit, it was a hostage.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Something pleasant and useless. Fishing. Reading something silly. Staring at the sea. I recommend staring at the sea, I'm a professional.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: A beginner who rests is quitting. A master who rests is resting. The difference is every day before it.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: How do I know I'm not quitting?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Because tomorrow you'll come back without thinking about it. That's the test. Tomorrow.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: If tomorrow is hard, then it was too soon. Come back the day after and we'll call it a lesson.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You spend the day doing nothing much. It feels strange, then nice, then strange again.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The next morning, you're up before the alarm. You're halfway through the milk round before you remember yesterday was a day off.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Ho ho. Passed.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Go on. The island will still be here.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A bright morning. Roshi is wearing a slightly nicer shirt than usual. It still has flowers on it.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: I've nothing left to teach you. That's not quite true, but it sounds good, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Then what happens now?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: The same thing as yesterday. Milk, shell, basics. Only now nobody has to tell you.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: Ho ho, I did consider a ceremony. Then I remembered I'd have to organise it.

then.speaker: ROSHI
then.text: I know you will. That's why we're here.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Do you know what a master is?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Someone who knows everything?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Nobody knows everything. I've been alive a very long time and I still can't work the remote.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: That's all a master is: a student who kept going after the teacher stopped watching.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Will you still be around?

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: I'm always around. This island isn't going anywhere, and neither am I. I'm too old to move.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Come back when you're stuck. Or when you're bored. Or when you want to beat me at chess, which you won't.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He holds out a hand. You shake it. His grip is far, far stronger than it looks.

lines.speaker: ROSHI
lines.text: Ho ho. Don't make that face. Come on, I'll buy lunch. You're paying.
